Resolves #19477

A callback throwing after a VDOM reply could strand later updates or reject another root whose vnode was already adopted. Settlement now releases the old flight before callbacks, captures its own completion phases, and handles failures per root. Callback dispatch drains detached snapshots while preserving work registered reentrantly. Sparse batching and emitted-root collision protection stay intact.

Evidence: deterministic real-instance failure controls and a real App/VDOM/Main browser guard. This leaf requires source/runtime validation; installed Fleet acceptance is separate.

Change class: restoration. `agent-preflight` is not hosted in Engine; normal commit hooks passed and shared baseline CI applies.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered `VdomLifecycle.spec.mjs`: throwing pre-update rejects the late request and its queued state renders. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered lifecycle and `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` controls: resolver/reject failures drain the claimed tail and retain no stale flight ownership. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered mixed-root, reentrant-flight, phase-ownership, reused-ID, destruction and initialization-through-common-settlement controls. |
| AC-4 | Existing sparse and collision controls remain green; [real-browser and diagnostic receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19477#issuecomment-6058284954). |

## Deltas from ticket

The existing callback manager needed snapshot isolation alongside the lifecycle fix: a throwing resolver otherwise loses its detached tail, and an old phase can consume a newly registered hook or waiter. The phase methods accept an already-detached snapshot; one-argument behavior remains compatible. Claimed snapshots reuse their existing arrays, with no new global tracking map.

The earlier initial-mount callback path never reaches this common settlement and is tracked independently in #19478. Its normal mount exception is retained. The failure originates inside shared settlement; consumers had no workaround to remove.

## Test Evidence

- The new lifecycle controls reproduce stranded late work and incorrect co-root rejection before repair; separate controls reproduce premature execution of a newer flight's phases.
- The original paired diagnostic now recovers both callback-failure cases while retaining its sparse-payload and collision controls.
- One exact-commit browser guard passes all six prior workloads, including the 500-input stream. This is a healthy-path compatibility/performance guard, not a fresh paired optimization claim. Details and timing bounds are in the [receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19477#issuecomment-6058284954).

---

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #19477 and its design authority: `promiseUpdate()` documents that a failing flight rejects parked promises, and `resolveVdomUpdate()` with the batch catch owns release. Also: the changed-file list (two core files, two existing specs); Grace's #19468 review (the destroyed-initiator co-root RA); your implementation notes in Memory Core; and `Base.destroy`'s release order (reject, unregister, trigger post-updates).
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** settlement must not throw past its own cleanup. Each root releases its own flight and settles every claimed callback, even when one throws. On failure it rejects only its own still-parked requests, never another root's adopted success. An old flight's phases must not consume a newer flight's hooks or waiters. Nothing in batching or insertion changes, and the tests use real instances with the single-thread VDOM setup.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `resolveVdomUpdate` snapshots and detaches the `preUpdateMap` and `postUpdateQueueMap` entries, unregisters before callbacks, and wraps each phase. Every later step is guarded by `Neo.getComponent(id) === me && !me.isDestroyed`, plus `!me.isVdomUpdating` before rejecting or retrying. `#settlePromiseCallbacks` drains the whole claimed list and rethrows the first error. `rejectPromiseCallbacks` and `triggerPostUpdates` detach before invoking, then drain.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. Every failure mode has a real-instance control that fails first, and the browser guard is reported as a compatibility check, not a speed claim.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:**
- *Weakness, accepted:* `executePreUpdates` and `triggerPostUpdates` now branch on `arguments.length`, so `f(id)` and `f(id, undefined)` do different things. That is documented and pinned by tests, and nothing forwards these methods today. A future forwarder with named parameters, though, would silently switch every caller to the snapshot path. Separate snapshot methods would describe themselves. This is not a Required Action.
- *Edge I checked:* the post-update queue is detached before callbacks run, but `Base.destroy()` releases only the live queue. A component destroyed during its own settlement would therefore strand the detached waiters. That cannot happen today: in `src`, the settled callbacks are only promise resolvers (no plain-callback `updateVdom` caller exists), so no synchronous user code runs in that window. A future plain-callback API would reopen it.
